title: EMR & EHR Data Extraction: How to Automate It Without an API
summary: Choose an EMR/EHR extraction method, collect provider productivity and billing data, and build a recurring report export in Skyvern without writing code.
body_markdown:
EMR/EHR data extraction is the process of taking information from electronic medical or health records so you can use it for reporting, billing, or analysis. That means exporting appointment records, pulling a provider’s procedure totals, or collecting payment data for a monthly report.


Getting all that information is time-consuming, repetitive work: sign into a portal, find the right report, select a date range, download the file, and copy the numbers into a spreadsheet. Then do it again for the next provider or location. Every reporting cycle brings another round of downloads and data entry.


This is exactly the kind of workflow we built Skyvern for (Skyvern's CEO here) . It can navigate your web-based EHR portal, select report filters, and download the files your team needs to review, without requiring an API integration.


In this article, I'll explain the main extraction methods and show you how to automate a recurring report export with Skyvern. I’ll walk through choosing a report, setting up the browser workflow, checking the results, and scheduling repeat runs without writing code.


Use Skyvern for the repeatable browser steps, then validate each export before downstream use.


## What data can you extract from an EMR or EHR?


- **Structured data:** patient and provider identifiers, appointments, coded diagnoses, procedures, lab values, charges and payments. These fields can often be returned in tabular exports or API responses.
- **Unstructured data:** narrative notes, scanned referrals and attached documents. Downloading a file preserves the source; turning its contents into fields may require OCR or language-model extraction and validation.


Start with the smallest dataset that answers the operational question. A provider productivity report may need provider IDs, service dates, procedure codes and work RVUs. It usually does not require copying every clinical note into the compensation workbook.


Structured exports contain fields and rows; notes and documents may need a separate extraction step. All examples shown are synthetic.


## Four ways to extract EHR data


Extraction route Useful for Check before choosing it


FHIR APIs and HL7 interfaces Structured exchange between authorized systems; supported clinical resources and events. Required fields, scopes, interfaces, refresh frequency and implementation terms.


Reporting databases Analytical queries and larger datasets, such as reports built with Epic Clarity. Database access, refresh lag, schema knowledge and an owner for the queries.


Report or CSV exports through the UI Recurring operational reports that staff already download. Browser automation can repeat the web steps. Browser access, export permissions, report filters, MFA and validation of each file.


Migration and archive services Moving historical records, retiring an EHR or retaining access to legacy charts. Export completeness, field mapping, attachments, reconciliation and retention requirements.


Use an existing API, interface or reporting database when it already supplies the required information reliably. For a report available only through a web interface, a browser workflow can handle the repeated navigation and download. It still needs an authorized account, a tested login path and checks on the result.


Compare the full cost of each approach: vendor terms, implementation, infrastructure, model usage, support and maintenance. There is no single API price or browser-automation cost that applies to every EHR and deployment.


### One-time migration vs ongoing extraction


An EHR conversion is a separate project involving historical records, mappings, attachments and reconciliation in the destination system. Recurring extraction keeps an operational process supplied with fresh reports. Skyvern’s role here is the repeatable browser work, such as downloading last month’s productivity report, rather than promising a complete EHR conversion.


## Extraction by EHR


Check the product version, hosting arrangement and permissions in your own environment. A vendor offering a web portal does not mean every reporting tool is available inside it.


### Epic data extraction: Reporting Workbench, Clarity and FHIR


Epic describes[Reporting Workbench and Clarity](https://www.epic.com/mu/?ref=skyvern.com) as different reporting tools: Reporting Workbench provides reports using real-time data, while Clarity extracts data into a separate reporting database. Your reporting team can identify the appropriate report and explain its refresh timing.


For an integration, review Epic’s[FHIR documentation](https://fhir.epic.com/Documentation?ref=skyvern.com) and the resources authorized for your application. For a recurring file export, confirm that the report and export controls are accessible in the browser. A workflow that depends on a native desktop or Citrix client needs a different access approach; do not assume a browser agent can operate it.


### eClinicalWorks data extraction


Separate a routine report download from a full EHI export.[eClinicalWorks’ published export details](https://www.eclinicalworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/ecw-onc-health-it-certification-details-and-additional-costs-disclosures-nov-2025.pdf?ref=skyvern.com) describe a single-patient export using its Windows EHI Export Utility and a patient-population export initiated through a support case. They also state that RCM customers need a separate export for RCM data.


For recurring operations, ask your administrator which billing or productivity reports your account can run and download through the web interface. Test that exact path. A Windows export utility and a browser report are different workflows, even when both return files.


### Oracle Health data extraction (Cerner)


Oracle Health Millennium supports[FHIR R4 APIs and bulk data access](https://docs.oracle.com/en/industries/health/millennium-platform-apis/guides.html?ref=skyvern.com) . Its[bulk export documentation](https://docs.oracle.com/en/industries/health/millennium-platform-apis/mfbda/api-bulk-export.html?ref=skyvern.com) describes supported patient resources, asynchronous jobs and downloadable files. Check those options before building a UI workflow for clinical data.


For a custom operational report, establish where staff run it, whether its interface is browser accessible, and which columns the export contains. Confirm provider attribution and date filters with the report owner before scheduling it.


### athenahealth data extraction


athenahealth offers[API and reporting options](https://www.athenahealth.com/developer-portal?ref=skyvern.com) for different workloads. APIs support integrations, while Data View provides access for analytics and bulk extraction. Its EHI Export feature covers patient and practice datasets. Confirm which products and fields are enabled for your organization before choosing the route.


If your team already downloads the needed report from athenaOne, document its filters and output format. Use browser automation for that repeatable web workflow when it fits your access and operational needs. Confirm whether the report includes the clinical, billing or collection data required, rather than assuming those datasets are interchangeable.


## Provider productivity, compensation and revenue cycle reporting


To automate provider compensation from EMR data, first automate the collection of the inputs your finance team has approved. That might be a monthly provider productivity report plus a billing or collections report. Keep the original exports so reviewers can trace a figure back to its source.


Work relative value units (wRVUs) measure the relative time and intensity associated with a physician service.[CMS distinguishes work RVUs from practice-expense and malpractice RVUs](https://www.cms.gov/help/pfs-quick-reference-search-guide?ref=skyvern.com) . A report’s work RVU total is not the same as total RVUs, billed charges, collections or compensation.


- **Define the period:** agree on service dates versus posting dates, the cutoff and how late entries are handled.
- **Identify the provider:** use stable IDs and confirm whether a report attributes activity to the rendering, supervising or billing provider.
- **Collect the right measures:** retain procedure codes, modifiers, units and the applicable RVU version when they are needed to explain the totals.
- **Reconcile exceptions:** flag duplicate rows, missing providers, reversals and unexpected changes before passing the dataset to finance.


Illustrative review sheet using synthetic data. Check provider IDs and duplicate periods, and keep wRVUs, charges and collections distinct; these are not compensation calculations.


Apply the organization’s approved compensation rules after validation, with a reviewer responsible for the result. Extraction should deliver traceable inputs; it should not infer a provider’s pay from a clinical note or substitute billed revenue for collected revenue.


The same approach can support revenue cycle management: collect charge, payment and accounts-receivable reports, then reconcile them with the appropriate downstream records. Related workflows include[insurance eligibility verification](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/automating-healthcare-insurance-eligibility-verification/) ,[EOB processing](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/automating-healthcare-claims-eob-processing-billing/) and[prior authorization](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/automate-healthcare-prior-authorization-insurance-portals/) . Each needs its own identifiers and validation rules.


## How to automate an EHR report export with Skyvern


This example collects a monthly provider productivity CSV from an authorized web portal. Use a test environment or synthetic records while building it, and approve the deployment and destination before introducing protected health information. The screenshots below show Skyvern’s documented controls using example workflows; they are not screenshots from a patient system.


### 1. Define the report and inputs


Run the report manually once and write down its exact name, required filters, expected columns and export format. Record how you know the file is complete, including whether there are multiple pages or locations. Decide who reviews a failed or unexpected result.


Open Skyvern and describe the job to Copilot. Ask it to build an agent that logs in, selects that report, exports a CSV and returns the file plus a short result summary. Name the portal URL and state that the workflow must not change patient records.


In Studio’s[Inputs panel](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/studio) , add values for the reporting period and provider or location filters. Reference those inputs in the workflow so the next run can use a new period without rewriting the instructions.


Use Inputs for values that change between runs. The documentation example shows a post-count input; use reporting dates and provider filters for this workflow.


[Source](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/studio) .


### 2. Connect the portal login


Use a saved login when Copilot asks to sign in, or configure a Login block with a stored credential. Keep the password out of the report prompt. The account must have permission to view the required report and export its data.


Configure MFA using[Skyvern’s credentials settings](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/credentials) . Authenticator-app codes can be generated from a stored TOTP key. Email codes can come from a connected inbox or a forwarding/push flow. SMS codes must be supplied through the supported push flow; entering a phone number alone does not give Skyvern access to the phone’s messages. Confirm the portal’s permitted authentication method and test an expired session.


Save the portal login separately from your prompt. Example interface from Skyvern’s credentials documentation.


### 3. Select the report and export it


Review the agent’s browser steps in Studio. Give the Browser Task the report name, filter values and a clear completion condition. For example:


“After login, open the Provider Productivity report. Set the service-date range to the supplied start and end dates and select the supplied location. Confirm the displayed filters. Download the full report as CSV, including all pages. Return the filename and displayed report totals. Stop if the report is unavailable, the filters cannot be confirmed or no export is produced. Do not edit any records.”


Use your portal’s actual report name and controls. A completed navigation step is not proof of a successful export: check that the file exists and corresponds to the requested period.


Configure the report and export instructions in a Browser Task. This documentation screenshot shows the configuration fields, not an EHR portal.


### 4. Test and validate the result


Review Copilot’s proposed changes and test the agent with the sample inputs. In the Run pane, open Outputs to inspect returned data, errors and downloaded files. Use the timeline or recording to investigate an incorrect filter or a missed download.


Compare the file against a manual export for the same inputs. Check required columns, provider IDs, dates, row counts and control totals. Include an empty period, a report with multiple pages and a failed login in testing. An empty report and a failed export must produce different outcomes.


Review results in the Run pane. This Skyvern documentation example uses public web data; your report export appears under Downloaded files.


### 5. Send approved results to a sheet or storage


Skyvern’s[integrations](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/integrations) include Google Sheets Read and Write blocks and a Cloud Storage block for Google Drive. Choose a destination your organization has approved for the dataset and configure its access controls before using it for PHI.


Keep the original export in approved storage. If you also write rows to a sheet, map each column explicitly and include a run ID, source report, reporting period and review status. Define a stable row or batch key so rerunning a period does not double-count activity. Test the delivery step as part of the workflow; downloading a CSV does not automatically populate a spreadsheet.


### 6. Schedule it and assign exception review


After the end-to-end test passes, use[Schedule in Studio](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/runs) to choose the frequency, timezone and input values. For monthly reports, confirm how the workflow determines the previous month; fixed test dates must not silently carry into every run.


Scheduling controls from


[Skyvern’s documentation](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/runs#schedule-an-agent) , shown with default values. Choose the cadence for your report and configure its date inputs separately.


Assign an owner to review failures, missing files and unexpected totals. Keep the source export and run reference with each batch. Recheck the workflow after report, portal or authentication changes, and measure both successful deliveries and the time spent resolving exceptions.


For an engineer connecting this workflow to another system, use the[Skyvern API reference](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/api-reference) .


## Protecting patient data during extraction


Treat the whole path as part of the deployment: the EHR account, browser, model endpoint, screenshots and recordings, downloaded files, storage and downstream integrations. A local browser does not by itself establish where every copy of the data goes.


Skyvern’s[healthcare page](https://www.skyvern.com/healthcare) describes the product as HIPAA compliant and SOC2 Type II. Confirm the deployment scope, security documentation and contractual terms for your organization before using PHI. SOC 2 assurance does not replace your HIPAA responsibilities.


Under[HHS guidance on cloud computing](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/health-information-technology/cloud-computing/index.html?ref=skyvern.com) , a cloud provider that creates, receives, maintains or transmits ePHI on a covered entity’s behalf is generally a business associate, even when it cannot decrypt the data. Put the required agreements in place. Self-hosting does not automatically remove obligations involving hosting, model or other service providers.


Build the workflow around the[HIPAA Security Rule’s safeguards](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/security/laws-regulations/index.html?ref=skyvern.com) :


- **Access:** restrict who can run the agent, change it, view its history and open its output. Use an EHR account with only the permissions needed.
- **Data protection:** configure encryption, retention and deletion across the approved environment, including logs, recordings, downloads and backups.
- **Auditability:** retain the run identity, report and filters used, access events, delivery outcome and reviewer decisions in the appropriate audit records.
- **Data minimization:** exclude patient identifiers and clinical detail when aggregate provider or operational data is sufficient.


Document who owns each control and how failed deliveries are recovered. The intended use, data flow and service-provider relationships determine the review; there is no universal “self-hosted means compliant” shortcut.


## Start with one recurring report


Choose a report your team already downloads and knows how to validate. Prove that the workflow uses the right filters, returns a complete file and reaches an approved destination. Then expand to another provider group, location or report.


Skyvern’s[EMR extraction and chart-review workflows](https://www.skyvern.com/healthcare) use browser automation to collect data where a web interface is the practical access route. Visual interpretation can reduce dependence on fixed selectors, but each portal still needs testing and monitoring. Start with a specific report and a measurable definition of success.


## Frequently asked questions


### What are the two types of data extraction?


The phrase can describe two different distinctions. Structured and unstructured describe the source data: coded fields and tables versus narrative notes and documents. Full and incremental describe the extraction strategy: copying the selected dataset in full versus collecting new or changed records. An EHR project may need both distinctions.


### Can you extract patient data from EHR systems without an API?


Yes, when an authorized user can access the required data through reports, exports or browser pages. A browser agent can repeat that workflow. It cannot grant permissions, expose fields absent from the interface or guarantee access to a desktop-only application.


### How do you automate provider compensation from EMR data?


Collect the approved productivity and billing reports on a defined schedule, reconcile provider identifiers and reporting periods, and flag exceptions. Pass the validated inputs to the compensation process your finance team owns. Keep wRVUs, charges, collections and pay calculations distinct.


### Can automation handle MFA and login timeouts?


It depends on the portal and how the credential is configured. Skyvern supports TOTP, connected or forwarded email codes, and pushed SMS codes. A code sent to a personal phone still needs an approved way to reach the workflow. Test that path, session expiration and any human approval requirement before relying on unattended runs.
